subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the assessment objectives.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: She apparently takes her own life
questions.explain: Her death is reported and understood to be suicide, the consequence of overwhelming guilt.

questions.q: Which character ultimately kills Macbeth in the final battle?
questions.explain: Macduff, who was "from his mother's womb untimely ripp'd", slays Macbeth and so fulfils the prophecy.

questions.q: Mr Birling's confident speeches about the Titanic being "unsinkable" are an example of what dramatic technique?
questions.explain: The audience knows the Titanic sank, making Birling's claims ironic and undermining his judgement.

questions.q: Mr Birling can be seen to represent which political viewpoint?
questions.explain: Birling champions individual profit and dismisses community, embodying capitalist values Priestley critiques.

questions.q: How was Sheila Birling responsible for Eva Smith's misfortune?
options: She had Eva dismissed from a shop out of jealousy
She reported her to the police
questions.explain: Sheila got Eva sacked from Milwards in a fit of jealous temper.

questions.q: In Jacobean England, the reigning monarch when Macbeth was written claimed descent from which character in the play?
questions.explain: James I traced his lineage to Banquo, which is why the witches show Banquo's descendants as future kings.

questions.q: Which character secretly marries Romeo and Juliet, hoping to end the feud?
questions.explain: Friar Lawrence weds them in secret, believing their union may reconcile the two families.

questions.q: Why does Romeo kill himself in the Capulet tomb?
options: He is mortally wounded by Paris
He believes Juliet is truly dead
He is ordered to by the Prince
questions.explain: Believing Juliet dead because he never received the Friar's message, Romeo drinks poison beside her.

questions.q: What does Macbeth hallucinate seeing before he murders Duncan?
options: A dagger leading him toward the chamber
questions.explain: He asks "Is this a dagger which I see before me?", a vision drawing him to commit the murder.

questions.q: What plan does Friar Lawrence give Juliet to avoid marrying Paris?
options: To drink a potion that makes her appear dead
To confess the secret marriage publicly
To run away to Mantua alone
questions.explain: He gives her a sleeping potion to feign death so she can later escape with Romeo.

questions.q: Who kills Mercutio in the play?
questions.explain: Tybalt fatally stabs Mercutio under Romeo's arm, prompting Mercutio's curse "A plague o' both your houses!".

questions.q: What unsettling twist occurs at the very end of the play?
options: A phone call announces a real inspector is coming to investigate a girl's death
questions.explain: After doubting Goole was real, the family learns a girl has died and a police inspector is on his way.
